planting.note: Plant container shrubs in late winter, spring, or fall in moist, well-drained soil in full sun; Shirobana is unusual among spirea in producing white, pink, and deep rose-red flower clusters simultaneously on the same plant.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, average soil in full sun; spirea flowers most heavily and holds the tightest habit in full sun, tolerating partial shade with looser growth and fewer blooms. Shirobana is a distinctive Japanese spirea that produces flat clusters of white, soft pink, and deep rose-red flowers all at once on the same shrub, an unusual multicolor effect rather than the single, uniform flower color typical of most spirea cultivars, blooming heavily in late spring with scattered rebloom through summer. Its fine-textured blue-green foliage provides an attractive backdrop to the mixed-color flower clusters and takes on russet tones in fall. Shear off spent flower clusters after the first flush to tidy the plant and encourage continued summer bloom, and cut the whole shrub back by a third in late winter every few years to renew vigorous growth.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in late winter, spring, or fall in moist, well-drained soil in full sun; Dakota Goldcharm is an especially compact, low-growing golden spirea bred for tight foundation plantings and edging.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, average soil in full sun for the brightest foliage color; spirea tolerates poor soil and drought once established but flowers and colors up best with a half-day or more of direct sun. Dakota Goldcharm stays notably lower and tighter than most golden-leaved spirea cultivars, forming a dense, mounded dwarf shrub with bright chartreuse-gold foliage that takes on orange-red tints in cool spring and fall weather, topped by small clusters of pink flowers in late spring. Its diminutive size fits low borders, rock gardens, and mass plantings where taller spirea would overwhelm the scale of the design. Shear off spent flowers after the main bloom flush to tidy the mound, and cut the whole plant back hard every few years in late winter to keep growth dense and prevent the center from opening up.

common_name: Double Play Big Bang Spirea (Bright Gold Reblooming Spirea)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in late winter, spring, or fall in moist, well-drained soil in full sun; best foliage color develops in full sun, and deadheading the first flush of flowers encourages the summer rebloom that gives this series its name.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, average soil in full sun; spirea tolerates poor soil and drought once established but colors up and flowers best with a full day of sun. Double Play Big Bang produces some of the brightest gold foliage in the reblooming Double Play spirea series, holding vivid yellow color through summer heat better than many older golden spirea cultivars, and topped by rounded clusters of pink flowers that appear in a heavy spring flush with continued rebloom through summer, especially with deadheading. Its compact, rounded habit fits foundation plantings, low borders, and mixed shrub beds without the sprawling size of older spirea varieties. Shear off spent flower clusters after the first bloom flush to encourage continued summer flowering, and cut the whole shrub back by up to a third every few years in late winter to renew dense, vigorous growth.

common_name: Double Play Candy Corn Spirea (Orange-Red New Growth Reblooming Spirea)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in late winter, spring, or fall in moist, well-drained soil in full sun; Candy Corn is grown chiefly for its multicolor spring foliage, which opens bright orange-red and matures through yellow to lime-green on the same branch.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, average soil in full sun for the strongest foliage color contrast. Double Play Candy Corn is grown primarily for its striking multicolor new growth, which emerges a vivid orange-red at the branch tips and matures backward through yellow to lime-green, giving each stem a gradient effect reminiscent of its namesake candy, with small clusters of pink flowers in late spring adding a secondary season of interest. New flushes of colorful growth continue to appear through the growing season, especially after a light shearing, keeping the color display going well past spring. Its compact, mounded habit suits low borders and foundation plantings, and cutting the whole shrub back hard every few years in late winter keeps growth dense and encourages the most vivid new color.

common_name: Double Play Painted Lady Spirea (Blue-Green Foliage Pink-Flowered Reblooming Spirea)
scientific_name: Spiraea japonica 'Painted Lady' (Double Play Painted Lady)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in late winter, spring, or fall in moist, well-drained soil in full sun; deadheading the first flush of flowers encourages the summer rebloom that gives the Double Play series its name.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, average soil in full sun; spirea tolerates poor soil and drought once established but flowers most reliably with a full day of direct sun. Double Play Painted Lady carries cool blue-green foliage rather than the gold or orange-red tones of other Double Play series members, providing a calmer backdrop for its clusters of rich pink flowers, which open in a heavy spring flush and continue reblooming through summer, especially when spent clusters are sheared off promptly. Its compact, rounded form fits foundation plantings and mixed borders where a reliable, long-blooming small shrub is needed without a bold foliage-color statement. Cut the whole shrub back by up to a third every few years in late winter to keep growth dense and renew vigorous flowering wood.
